text:
mike.c: sec-bot just flagged unusual usage for internal token `service-batch-runner-prod` — calls from three distinct external IPs in the last 30m :eyes:
sec-bot: ALERT: anomalous_token_usage detected for token=service-batch-runner-prod, src_ips=[54.210.23.11, 3.120.45.2, 18.196.2.9], first_seen=1801234512, events=42
jess.k: copying logs now. mike, do we know which job/process uses that token?
mike.c: it's used by the nightly batch job that imports partner data — normally runs from our CI pool (10.x.x.x) and from our GKE egress IPs. these src_ips are public cloud ranges we don't use.
ranjit.s: 1) immediate containment: revoke the token or disable it? 2) we need to avoid killing any customer-facing flows. Which systems depend on it?
sarah.security: containment first. create a short-lived deny rule for those src_ips at the WAF/ingress and mark the token as compromised. then rotate token after we verify no essential customer traffic will break.
jess.k: running quick audit query against audit-logs to see calls authenticated by that token in the last 72h:
```
resource.type=\"k8s_container\"
jsonPayload.auth.token_id=\"service-batch-runner-prod\"
| select timestamp, src_ip, user_agent, request_path
| limit 200
```
(found ~40 events, most are POST /internal/ingest)
mike.c: confirmed: 6 unique pod names, all from a single CI pipeline `infra/partner-imports` — but the three external IPs show up in traces for the same token after 15:12 UTC.
tia.cs: @jess.k should we notify affected partners? any customer-visible errors?
jess.k: no 5xx spikes in public API metrics. looks internal-only so far, but need to confirm none of these jobs carry partner data outbound.
ranjit.s: action plan: 1) block those src IPs at edge, 2) create new token with minimal scope, 3) rotate CI to new token behind KMS (Cloud KMS) and do rollout canary for batch jobs, 4) retros and repo scan for leaked creds. I'm going to prepare the rotate playbook.
mike.c: I'm going to hit the edge block now and tag the token as compromised in the secrets store. will not fully delete yet until new token is deployed to avoid long downtime. :lock:
ops-oncall: applied temporary deny for 54.210.23.11 and 3.120.45.2 at the edge; 18.196.2.9 is already blocked by ASN policy. watching.
sec-bot: ACTION: token_status=marked_compromised, incident_id=INC-2026-0456
sarah.security: make sure we capture the KV cache/redis traces and S3 PUTs for that token — run S3 access logs query for that token as well. if any customer PII left, we escalate to privacy.
jess.k: running git history scan for token string across repos (quick grep):
```
for r in $(cat repos.txt); do git -C $r grep -n \"service-batch-runner-prod\" || true; done
```
no direct hits so far. also kicked off `git-secrets --scan` across org.
ranjit.s: we'll generate a new token via KMS envelope encryption. steps: create new key version, create secret in secrets manager encrypted with KMS key, grant CI runner access via short-lived RBAC role. limit token scopes to `ingest:write` only and add TTL 24h rotation for initial rollout.
mike.c: created issue in infra repo with rollout steps and canary schedule: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/4712 (internal link)
tia.cs: pinging CS to prep a templated note in case a partner asks. so far no evidence of data exfil.
ops-oncall: rotated token on canary runners to `service-batch-runner-prod-v2` and forced new secret version in Vault. bulk rotate scheduled 30m after green canary. monitoring ingest pipeline errors.
sec-bot: AUDIT: captured 42 events, wrote findings to /shared/sec/incidents/INC-2026-0456/logs.log
jess.k: post-containment checklist: - confirm no customer data exfil - full repo scan - rotate token(s) - enforce repo-level pre-commit hooks + git-secrets - add alert for token use from non-approved egress ranges - add RBAC change proposal to reduce token privileges
sarah.security: also recommend adding KMS key rotation and HSM-backed KEKs for service tokens used in prod; file policy PR for least-privilege defaults.
ranjit.s: assigning follow-ups: (1) infra: rotate all service tokens tied to `partner-imports` pipeline (ranjit) (2) devex: add git-secrets and pre-commit hooks org-wide (jess) (3) security: postmortem and customer comms template (sarah) (4) cs: readiness check (tia)
mike.c: quick note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis — CI runner leaked token via misconfigured job env var that printed to public logs in last deploy. need to confirm.
ops-oncall: can confirm one job had `echo $TOKEN` in a failing step around 15:05 UTC; that job logs were forwarded to an S3 bucket that had lax ACLs historically. I'm opening a follow-up to lock bucket ACLs now.
sarah.security: sounding likely. make sure we include S3 ACL fix and pre-commit secrets blocking in the postmortem.
sec-bot: update: token service-batch-runner-prod status=disabled, disabled_by=ops-oncall, disabled_at=1801234578
mike.c: thanks team. after bulk rotate and S3 ACL fix we'll schedule postmortem and RCA. tagging INC-2026-0456 and moving to post-detection phase. :white_check_mark:
ranjit.s: will also propose an RBAC change to require tokens have owner and expiry metadata and disallow long-lived tokens by default.
ops-oncall: monitoring dashboards show no downstream failures; will keep watch for 2 hours then close the incident if stable.
tia.cs: prepping CS note in draft: \"We identified a short-lived exposure of an internal service token used for partner imports. No customer-facing impact detected. We've rotated the token, tightened access controls, and are conducting a full review.\" will share for review.
sarah.security: adding incident to Q-end security review and scheduling follow-up remediation sprint items. thanks all.
